newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe Hartley Platinum on track for June start.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe Hartley Platinum on track for June start.

text.p: Zimbabwe's largest mining investment Hartley Platinum mine is on track for a mid-June production start after a five-month setback, general manager Colin Palethorpe told Reuters on Friday.
"We are still forecasting first production in June, barring any unforeseen circumstances," Palethorpe said.
Heavy rains, in addition to delays in breaking ground and training miners, were to blame for the delay, he said.
"The rain does have an effect. The construction of the refinery is crucial to first production and this (rain) has been part of its delay," Palethorpe said.
The mine was initially forecast to produce last November and the refinery completed by April this year.
The cost of the Hartley project -- a joint venture between Australian mining giant Broken Hill Proprietary Ltd and Delta Gold NL -- is an estimated $287 million, Palethorpe said.

When it reaches full production of 180,000 tonnes of ore by September 1998, Hartley is expected to have platinum output of 150,000 ounces, 110,000 ounces of palladium, 11,500 ounces of rhodium and 23,000 ounces of gold.
Hartley would raise to 3.5 percent Zimbabwe's contribution to world platinum production.
